Need the Wikipedia minimum perigee and Kipchoge’s record marathon time, then compute distance ÷ pace and round to the nearest 1000 hours. I’ll retrieve the source data first.


I’m checking the relevant Wikipedia entries for the exact values before calculating.



I’ll search for the exact Wikipedia figures needed for the calculation.
```python
search_results = await web_search("Wikipedia Moon minimum perigee Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record time", max_results=5)
print(search_results)
```
The search results will identify the specific Wikipedia values; I’ll use those exact figures and then calculate the travel time.
```python
print(search_results)
```
```python
search_results = await web_search("site:en.wikipedia.org Moon perigee minimum km Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record 2:01:09", max_results=5)
print(search_results)
```
I’ll fetch the two Wikipedia pages directly to avoid relying on search-result snippets.
```python
moon_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon", max_chars=20000)
kipchoge_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge", max_chars=12000)
print({"moon": moon_page, "kipchoge": kipchoge_page})
```
I’m extracting the relevant numerical snippets from the fetched pages.
```python
calc_check = await calculator("(356400 / (42195 / (2 + 1/60 + 9/3600))) / 3600")
print(calc_check)
```
The required inputs are the minimum lunar perigee and Kipchoge’s 2:01:09 marathon pace; I’ll verify the figures in the knowledge search before finalizing the rounded result.
```python
kb_check = await knowledge_search_knowledge("Moon Wikipedia minimum perigee Eliud Kipchoge marathon world record", scope="all")
print(kb_check)
```
17
